note: How content moves, renders, and gets looked at. The four tables live beside this file as CSVs: docs/routes-modes.csv (the delivery modes pages/toss-render.html accepts), docs/routes-routes.csv (the toss routes that map a content type to the page that renders it), docs/showing-mechanisms.csv (which link reaches which kind of change, and what each one misses), and docs/routes-kinds.csv (what the subject IS: how each kind is recognized, the viewer mode it opens in, and the units a note can be pinned to inside it, which is the showing block's subject axis read one level down). What stays here is what is not a table: the address grammar, the parameter precedence, and the frame the showing block puts around the mechanisms. Split on 2026-08-18, when the last three registries sharing this file became CSVs of their own; nothing here is a registry any more. The kinds table joined them on 2026-08-31.
precedence: Every parameter below is read fragment first, query as fallback: toss-render for its own params, and the renderer pages through lib/kits/url-params.js. Put a payload in the fragment, which never reaches a server and so escapes the roughly 8KB cap the Pages edge enforces with a 414 (PR #165). An address is short, so either form works, and a routed toss delivers ?src= through toss-render's params shim rather than over the wire. The same precedence decides a whole HALF of an address, not just one key: when show-repo's shell frames a promoted page (?app=<slug>), the shell owns the query and the framed page owns the fragment, with ?on= as that page query fallback. One rule, no reserved-name list on either side, which is what keeps it from rotting as the shell keys and a framed page keys both grow in different repos. lib/kits/url-params.js subject() implements it.

grammar.role: One way to name a file in any repo, at any ref. The ':' before the path is unambiguous because git forbids ':' in ref names; no @ref means the repo's default branch.

usedBy.where: a repo's pages catalog and stage.files

showing.note: Getting a subject in front of a viewer. Three independent variables decide the mechanism, and conflating them is what made this hard to state: WHAT the subject is, WHICH version of it, and WHO is opening the link. `preview` is not a topic, it is one value of `version`.

picker.note: The mechanism is derivable rather than remembered: it follows from which files a branch changed. show-repo knows a branch's changed files already.

rules.when: the repo's manifest names an app that frames its pages, and the change is under a declared view or the app's own folder
